newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - March 27.

text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Thursday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) plans to present bill in 1999 to abolish six special public corporations.
-- LDP, Social Democratic Party (SDP) and New Party Sakigake plan to set limits on drug prices as part of medical insurance reform.
-- China expresses determination to further open its markets in the meeting with U.S. Vice President Al Gore.
-- Bank of Japan is ready to offer sufficient credit to help Nippon Credit Bank.
-- Government plans to invite warring Afghan factions to Tokyo for peace talks.
-- A strong earthquake shook the southern Japanese island of Kyushu.
-- Six universities use livers from brain-dead donors from the United States for drug research.
-- Lower House is expected to vote on organ transplant bill in April.
-- U.S. Vice President Al Gore and Chinese President Jiang Zemin confirm mutual visits of leaders.
